{{Short description|American men's college basketball season}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=August 2024}} {{Infobox college sports team season | year = 2025–26 | team = Virginia Cavaliers | sport = basketball | logo = Virginia Cavaliers wordmark.svg | logo_size = 250 | conference = Atlantic Coast Conference | short_conf = ACC | CoachRank = 15 | APRank = 17 | record = 30–6 | conf_record = 15–3 | head_coach = [[Ryan Odom]] | hc_year = 1st | assoc_coach = [[Griff Aldrich]] | ahc_year = 1st | asst_coach1 = Matt Henry | ac1_year = 1st | asst_coach2 = Bryce Crawford | ac2_year = 1st | asst_coach3 = [[Darius Theus]] | ac3_year = 1st | arena = [[John Paul Jones Arena]] | champion = | tourney=[[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] | tourney_result = Second round }} {{2025–26 ACC men's basketball standings}} The '''2025–26 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Virginia]] during the [[2025–26 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. They were led by first-year head coach [[Ryan Odom]] following the departure of interim head coach [[Ron Sanchez]]. They played their home games at [[John Paul Jones Arena]] in [[Charlottesville, Virginia]], as members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. The Cavaliers began the season with four straight wins before traveling to [[White Sulphur Springs, West Virginia]] to participate in the [[Greenbrier Tip-Off]]. They won their first game of the tournament to extend their winning streak to six games. The streak ended in the final of the tournament with an eight-point loss to [[2025–26 Butler Bulldogs men's basketball team|Butler]]. The Cavaliers picked up where they left off, winning their next three straight games, including a victory at [[2025–26 Texas Longhorns men's basketball team|Texas]] in the [[ACC–SEC Challenge]]. These victories saw them enter the [[2025–26 NCAA Division I men's basketball rankings|AP poll]] at number twenty-four. They won three further non-conference games against non-Power 4 opponents to rise to twenty first in the rankings. They began ACC play with a [[Virginia–Virginia Tech men's basketball rivalry|rivalry]] game against [[2025–26 Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball team|Virginia Tech]]. The game went to triple [[Overtime (sports)#Basketball|overtime]] and the Cavaliers lost by ten points. The team went on a five game winning streak after the loss, which included three road victories, including ove at twentieth-ranked [[2025–26 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Louisville]]. They rose to fourteenth in the rankings before losing by five points to twenty-second ranked [[2025–26 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]]. They fell to seventeenth after the loss, but went on a nine-game winning streak to ascend to eleventh. The streak included one non-conference game, a victory over [[2025–26 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|Ohio State]]. They did not defeat a ranked team over the stretch, but did notch a double overtime victory at [[2025–26 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team|Notre Dame]], along with three other road victories. The streak was broken at top-ranked [[2025–26 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]], 51–77. The Cavaliers defeated [[2025–26 Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball team|Wake Forest]] by five points and they won their rivalry re-match with Virginia Tech by four points to end the regular season. They were ranked tenth in the AP poll entering the postseason. The Cavaliers finished the season 30–6 overall and 15–3 in [[2025–26 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in second place. As the second seed in the [[2026 ACC men's basketball tournament|2026 ACC tournament]], they earned a double-bye into the Quarterfinals where they defeated seven seed [[2025–26 NC State Wolfpack men's basketball team|NC State]]. They advanced over third seed [[2025–26 Miami Hurricanes men's basketball team|Miami]] in the Semifinals. They could not win the tournament as they lost to top seed and top ranked Duke in the Final, 70–74. The Cavaliers earned an at-large bid to the [[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] and were the three-seed in the [[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament#Midwest regional – Chicago, Illinois|Midwest region]]. They were ranked ninth in the AP Poll released prior to the tournament. They defeated fourteen-seed [[2025–26 Wright State Raiders men's basketball team|Wright State]] in the First Round before being upset by six-seed and twenty-third ranked [[2025–26 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]] by six-points to end their season. ==Previous season== {{main|2024–25 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team}} With the last-minute retirement of [[Tony Bennett (basketball)|Tony Bennett]] and the appointing of interim head coach [[Ron Sanchez]], the Cavaliers started the season 3–0, including a ten-point victory over [[2024–25 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]] in the Hall of Fame Series. They then traveled to the Bahamas to participate in the [[Bahamas Championship|Baha Mar Hoops Championship]] where their fortunes changed. They lost in the semifinals to eleventh-ranked [[2024–25 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]] 64–42 and in the third place game against twenty second-ranked [[2024–25 St. John's Red Storm men's basketball team|St. John's]] 80–55. They won two games against non-Power 4 opponents before losing their [[ACC–SEC Challenge]] game against thirteenth-ranked [[2024–25 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]] 87–69. They followed that with a loss in their ACC opener against [[2024–25 SMU Mustangs men's basketball team|SMU]]. They finished their non-conference slate 2–1, with a loss against twenty first-ranked [[2024–25 Memphis Tigers men's basketball team|Memphis]]. They closed the 2024 portion of their schedule with an ACC win over [[2024–25 NC State Wolfpack men's basketball team|NC State]]. The Cavaliers had a rough start to the 2025 portion of the schedule, as they went on a five-game losing streak. The streak included two losses to [[2024–25 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Louisville]], and losses in California to [[2024–25 Stanford Cardinal men's basketball team|Stanford]] and [[2024–25 California Golden Bears men's basketball team|California]], and a loss in a rematch with SMU. They broke the streak by going 2–2 in their next four games. This streak included a loss in their [[Virginia–Virginia Tech rivalry|rivalry]] game against [[2024–25 Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball team|Virginia Tech]]. The team went 4–2 over their next six games, which included a three game winning streak. They defeated [[2024–25 Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball team|Pittsburgh]], [[2024–25 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team|Georgia Tech]], [[2024-25 Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball team|Wake Forest]], and won the rivalry rematch with Virginia Tech. However, they lost to third-ranked [[2024-25 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] and at [[2024-25 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]]. They lost to thirteenth-ranked [[2024-25 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team|Clemson]] and defeated [[2024-25 Florida State Seminoles men's basketball team|Florida State]] by three points in their next two games. The Cavaliers lost the regular season finale to [[2024-25 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]] 84–70. The Cavaliers finished the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|season]] 15–16 and 8–12 in [[2024–25 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in a five-way tie for ninth place. The team finished atop the five-way tiebreaker and were the ninth seed in the [[2025 ACC men's basketball tournament|2025 ACC tournament]]. They faced eighth-seed Georgia Tech in the First Round. Despite defeating the Yellow Jackets during the regular season, they were defeated 66–60 in the tournament. They were not invited to the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] or the [[2025 National Invitation Tournament|NIT]].
